papers.title: Distinct effects of Atg3 and Atg10 on Autophagosome Formation in Yeast
papers.abstract: Autophagosome formation involves two E2 enzymes: Atg3, which conjugates Atg8 to the lipid phosphatidylethanolamine, and Atg10, which conjugates Atg12 to Atg5. Although both are required for autophagy, it is unclear exactly what roles these pathways play in the process of autophagosome formation. We used baker's yeast expressing mutant versions of both Atg3 and Atg10 that reduce, but do not eliminate, their activity to better understand their effects on Atg8 lipidation, autophagic flux, and the size and number of autophagosomes formed during nitrogen starvation. We found that while Atg3 primarily affects Atg8 lipidation and autophagosome size, Atg10 has less of an effect on Atg8 lipidation and primarily controls autophagosome number. This demonstrates that these two enzymes have distinct mechanistic roles in autophagosome formation, and implies an as-of-yet undiscovered function for the Atg12-Atg5 conjugate.

papers.title: Extending intravitreal retention of CNTF via fusion to the HA-binding protein VG1
papers.abstract: Glaucoma is the leading cause of permanent blindness worldwide. Vision loss in glaucoma stems from the loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGC). Ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) has been shown to protect RGCs in pre-clinical models of glaucoma. However, CNTF has a short ocular retention time following intraocular injections due to rapid diffusion. To address this, we developed a fusion protein between CNTF and the hyaluronic acid- (HA) binding G1 domain of endogenous extracellular matrix (ECM) protein, versican (VG1; CNTF-VG1). We hypothesize that a CNTF-VG1 protein will have an extended ocular retention time compared to CNTF due to HA-binding with endogenous vitreous-HA. We demonstrate that CNTF-VG1 non-covalently binds HA with high affinity and is bioactive. We show that the vitreous and thermal stability of CNTF-VG1 can be significantly increased through co-formulation with HA. In an in vivo pharmacodynamic study, we show that VG1 significantly increases the window of neuroprotective JAK/STAT3 pathway activation in un-injured mice (C57BL/6J, female) retina. Finally, we close our work by showing that CNTF is neuroprotective of primary mouse cortical neurons in an acute H2O2 cytotoxicity model. Taken together, our work demonstrates the potential of HA-binding domain VG1 to improve the ocular retention of neuroprotective CNTF following intraocular injection.

papers.title: Cortical ER-PM contact sites promote nuclear ER membrane integrity and mitotic nuclear segregation
papers.abstract: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) extends from the nuclear envelope through the cytoplasm to the cell cortex, where it contacts the plasma membrane (PM) at ER-PM membrane contact sites (MCSs). We hypothesized that as contiguous extensions of nuclear ER these cortical ER (cER) attachments to the PM might dampen shearing stresses on the nuclear envelope and help orchestrate nuclear ER dynamics. Although individual cER-PM tether proteins promote cER inheritance during mitosis, our findings reveal that removing all cER-PM tethers collectively disrupts nuclear envelope membrane integrity. In yeast {triangleup}-super-tether ({triangleup}-s-tether) cells lacking seven cER-PM tethers, cER detachment causes membrane blisters and nuclear envelope ruptures; however, individual tether deletions or ER stress do not disrupt nuclear containment. Despite the extensive nuclear envelope lesions in {triangleup}-s-tether cells, ESCRT-III (Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport-III)-mediated membrane repair sustains cell viability. The loss of nuclear integrity, however, appears to disrupt genomic repair and promotes spontaneous mutation; separately, nuclear inheritance is also disrupted. Without cER-PM MCSs, cortical actin depolarization and defects in nucleopodia impair mitotic nuclear dynamics and segregation, which triggers a Spindle Position Checkpoint (SPOC) cell-cycle delay. That cER-PM MCSs serve as dual-function hubs for the preservation of nuclear envelope integrity is indicated by two independent mechanisms capable of rescuing the observed nuclear membrane defects: the restoration of phospholipid metabolism or the re-establishment of nonspecific cER-PM contact.

papers.title: Coarse-tuning to improve a protein foundation model for a domain of proteins: the example of outer membrane beta barrels
papers.abstract: Foundation models for proteins have shown great potential in addressing a wide range of challenges in computational molecular biology. State-of-the-art models are trained on large and diverse corpora of protein sequences, enabled by self-supervised training. The models are then used in transfer learning and the embeddings they calculate are used in supervised downstream tasks. We propose a novel focusing mechanism for foundation models, which we call 'coarse-tuning'. In coarse-tuning, we further update the model, using a defined yet unlabeled, dataset to enhance its performance in a specific domain. We demonstrate this approach using Outer Membrane Beta Barrels (OMBBs) - proteins that are found in the distinct biophysical environment of the outer membrane. Our results show that coarse-tuned models outperform the original foundation model when applied to various transfer learning tasks. Additionally, we study the embeddings generated by the coarse-tuned models and compare them to those from the original foundation model, including an investigation of the learned attention matrices via contact map predictions. Our work suggests that a medium-sized dataset (fewer than 100,000 protein sequences) is sufficient to effectively specialize a foundation model to a specific domain, enhancing its utility for domain-specific applications.

papers.title: Self-organized criticality in a mammalian RNA-interference circuit
papers.abstract: Living systems have been argued to operate near critical points, but their relevance at the cellular level is poorly understood. Critical states allow for a high sensitivity to external inputs and maximal information transfer and display fluctuations at all scales. Critical points are very special, and require the fine tuning of a control parameter, which is hard to reconcile with the robustness of living cells. Self-organized criticality (SOC) proposes that feedback, rather than tuning, brings a system to its critical point. Here we show that RNA interference, in which messenger RNAs compete for shared silencing machinery and so queue for service, together with negative feedback gives rise to SOC in mammalian cells. In a synthetic circuit, a protein repressor whose mRNA competes with the mRNA of a fluorescent reporter that it represses senses the congestion of the queue, closing the feedback loop. Theory and stochastic simulations show that the loop holds the queue near its critical point despite changes in its parameters, and that expression becomes intermittent, with scale-free bursts. Measurements in human cell lines show the predicted power-law distributions of single-cell fluorescence. RNA interference could thus support engineered SOC in animal cells and may also contribute to SOC in natural systems.

papers.title: Associative Learning and Memory Erasure in a Synthetic Multicellular System
papers.abstract: Learning is a basic form of adaptation that organisms display from neural systems to single cells. In associative learning, the pairing of two stimuli lets one of them evoke the response to the other. Engineering this behavior in a living cell is difficult, because coincidence detection, memory, and conditional readout must be wired into a single regulatory network. Here we build a consortium of five E. coli strains that distributes the operations of associative learning and communicates through one diffusible quorum-sensing signal. The same signal acts as the memory trace. One strain detects the coincidence of the two inputs, a second maintains the memory through positive feedback in the shared medium, a third reads it out on the conditioned stimulus, a fourth reports the unconditioned response, and a fifth erases the memory on command. We show experimentally that the assembled consortium learns the association, since a stimulus that is silent before training evokes a strong response after pairing. Memory is retained through a medium exchange in which both stimuli are removed, and then the conditioned stimulus alone evokes the response. The reporter is not produced without its input. An erase command returns the response to the background. A population model of the consortium accounts for the sequence of responses and gives design rules for writing, retention, and erasure, and a trade-off in storing memory in a shared extracellular signal. Distributing the operations over strains makes each of them separately tunable and testable and provides a route to microbial communities that learn from their history.

papers.title: An anaerobic cell-free protein synthesis formulation for the in vitro study of oxygen sensitive proteins
papers.abstract: Anaerobic microbes harbor unique enzymes and metabolic pathways with potential biotechnological applications, yet these microbes remain difficult to study and engineer. Research is limited by the labor-intensive workflows required to maintain anoxic environments and the lack of genetic tools available for non-model anaerobes. Here, we present an anaerobic cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) platform for the in vitro study of oxygen-sensitive enzymes. This study establishes two methods for conducting anaerobic CFPS, achieving an anoxic environment by (1) sparging with inert gas or (2) lyophilizing to remove oxygenated water. We show the functionality of our anaerobic CFPS formulation by producing oxygen-independent fluorescent protein reporters and a [4Fe-4S] cluster pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) with a specific activity of 5.2 {+/-} 0.3 x 10-4 U/{micro}L cell-free extract. This highly modular platform will allow study of diverse oxygen-sensitive proteins and requires only minor modifications to commonly used CFPS workflows.

papers.title: Single Nucleus Profiling Reveals Rewired Tumor-Immune-Stromal Cell Communication in Plasmacytoid Urothelial Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Plasmacytoid urothelial carcinoma (PUC) is an aggressive histologic subtype of bladder cancer associated with worse patient outcomes and therapeutic response compared to conventional urothelial carcinoma (CUC). While recent work has demonstrated metastatic lymph nodes from PUC tumors have an inflamed phenotype, how the tumor microenvironment (TME) and crosstalk between tumor, stromal, and immune cells in primary PUC bladder tumors differs from those in CUC remains poorly understood. The impact of these differences on response to immunotherapy is also unknown. To understand TME differences between CUC and PUC and their impact on cell signaling, we performed single nucleus RNA sequencing on PUC and CUC tumors, as well as Xenium spatial transcriptomics on a mixed CUC / PUC tumor. We identified increased signaling between PUC-enriched, CDH1-low urothelial cells, immunosuppressive lipid-associated macrophages, and SFRP2+/CTHRC1+ fibroblasts in PUC tumors compared to CUC. Spatial transcriptomics identified increased macrophage infiltration in PUC histology and colocalization of PUC tumor cells, immunosuppressive macrophages, and SFRP2+ fibroblasts. Taken together, this study delineates PUC architecture and demonstrates interplay CDH1-low tumor cells, EMT, and immunosuppressive macrophages, identifying possible therapeutic vulnerabilities in PUC.

papers.title: A dynamic phosphoproteome reveals stage-specific regulation of cytokinesis in Leishmania
papers.abstract: Leishmania parasites undergo extensive morphological and metabolic remodelling during their transition from motile insect promastigotes to non-motile intracellular amastigotes, yet how dynamic protein kinase signalling drives this process remains poorly understood. Here, we present a high-resolution temporal phosphoproteome of L. mexicana promastigote to axenic amastigote differentiation, profiling 16,495 phosphosites on 3,101 proteins across seven developmental time points and identifying 5,795 dynamically regulated sites. This temporal map reveals stage-specific signalling programs, including regulated sites in MPK2 and non-regulated sites in MRK1, protein kinases known to be essential for amastigote differentiation. Using analogue-sensitive (AS) chemical genetics, we show that acute inhibition of either kinase in axenic amastigotes disrupts the spatial coordination of cleavage furrow ingression with nuclear and kinetoplast segregation, revealing essential cytokinesis roles obscured in constitutive gene deletions. Despite generating similar cytokinesis phenotypes, genetic over-expression and cellular localisation analyses demonstrate that MPK2 and MRK1 act through spatially segregated signalling pathways. Time-resolved phosphoproteomics upon MPK2 inhibition places its activity upstream of cytoskeletal remodelling networks. Importantly, we show that the stage-specific requirement for MPK2 is defined by the parasite's morphology: while motile promastigotes tolerate MPK2 inhibition, genetic ablation of flagellar motility sensitises them to loss of MPK2 activity. Thus, flagellar motility acts as a mechanical buffer during promastigote division, explaining why non-motile amastigotes are vulnerable to MPK2 inhibition. Together, our findings provide a systems level framework for Leishmania signalling and demonstrate that cellular architecture and biomechanics dictate protein kinase dependency across developmental stages of the parasite.

papers.title: Single-cell Transcriptome-Proteome-PTMome(x8)-Metabolome (scTPPM) co-profiling decodes multimodal regulation during mouse oocyte meiosis
papers.abstract: Single-cell multi-omics technology is crucial for comprehensive characterization of cellular molecular features. Despite recent advances in single-cell multi-omics approaches, co-profiling of nucleic acids, proteins, metabolites, and post-translational modifications (PTMs) within the same cell individuals remains major challenges. Here, we developed a single-cell transcriptome, proteome, PTMome, and metabolome (scTPPM) profiling approach, enabling simultaneous analysis of transcriptomes, proteomes, eight types of PTMs (e.g., phosphorylation, methylation, ubiquitination, O_GlcNAc, acetylation, crotonylation, lactylation, and succinylation), and metabolomes in individual cells. We demonstrated the scTPPM's performance in tumor cell lines and oocyte samples, reaching total identification and quantification of 27,668 genes, 4,847 proteins, 1,508 PTM sites, and 680 metabolites in single mouse oocytes. We profiled previously-uncharacterized dynamic crosstalk among the entire metabolic pathways from metabolic enzyme expression and regulation to metabolite-mediated post-translational modifications during oocyte maturation. In summary, scTPPM provided an effective workflow for multi-omics co-profiling in single cells, enabling multi-layered insights into complex regulatory network.

papers.title: Intercellular trafficking of latent TGF-β1 converts integrin expressing cells into signaling relays
papers.abstract: TGF-{beta}1 is secreted as a latent complex tethered to the cell surface by milieu molecules such as GARP, and its activation requires direct engagement by integrin-expressing cells. How this interaction converts the latent complex into signaling-competent growth factor (GF) remains unclear. Here we show that contact between GARP/TGF-{beta}1-presenting cells and cells expressing integrin V{beta}6 or V{beta}8 triggers rapid trogocytosis of the latent complex, both in transfected cells and two cancer cell lines that natively express these integrins. Independent labeling of the prodomain, GF, and GARP shows that all three components are co-transferred to the integrin-expressing cell, and a TGF-{beta}1 mutant (RGE) that cannot bind integrins shows little transfer. Using a reporter system that tracks pathway activation in presenting, integrin-expressing, and bystander cells, we find that GF-neutralizing antibodies block downstream signaling more effectively in bystander cells than in the first two cell types that participate in trogocytosis. Blocking cleavage between the prodomain and the GF blocks signaling in bystander cells while still permitting signaling in trogocytosing cell types. Finally, we integrin-expressing cells that have taken up latent TGF-{beta}1 by trogocytosis can activate it and signal to bystander cells after the TGF-{beta}1 cells are removed, indicating that trogocytosis converts integrin-expressing cells into TGF-{beta} signaling relays. These findings identify a role for trogocytosis in regulating the specificity of TGF-{beta}1 activation and signaling, and reveal a novel function of integrins in controlling protein localization.

papers.title: An ssRNA Phage Single-gene Lysis Protein Targeting MraY Reveals Convergent Evolution Across the RNA-DNA Phage Boundary
papers.abstract: Small lytic phages of the ssRNA Leviviricetes and ssDNA Microviricetes achieve host lysis by expression of a single protein, designated as an Sgl protein. Four ssRNA Sgls have been shown to inhibit steps in peptidoglycan biosynthesis: three target MurJ, the Lipid II flippase, and one targets MurA, the committed step of the pathway. A fifth Sgl, the E protein of the canonical ssDNA microvirus {varphi}X174, inhibits MraY, which catalyzes the synthesis of the first lipid-linked intermediate. This inhibition requires SlyD, a cytoplasmic FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase. The Sgl of the Caulobacter ssRNA phage {varphi}Cb5 (Cebevirus halophobicum) has not been characterized. Here, we present physiological evidence that Sgl{varphi}Cb5 targets MraY. Moreover, we show that, despite the absence of detectable sequence similarity, Sgl{varphi}Cb5 shares several features with the {varphi}X174 E protein, including the distribution of hydrophobic and charged residues, a proposed N-out, C-in membrane topology, and retention of lytic activity in an Sgl{varphi}Cb5 -LacZ fusion. Furthermore, expression of the Caulobacter cytoplasmic FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase CC2799 enhances Sgl{varphi}Cb5 -mediated lysis in E. coli. These parallels between Sgl function in a DNA phage and an RNA phage either represent remarkably consonant convergent evolution or some evolutionary cross-over event for which there is currently no precedent.

papers.title: PKR inhibition prevents maladaptive responses to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in early-onset dystonia DYT-PRKRA.
papers.abstract: DYT-PRKRA is a rare, childhood-onset dystonia caused by mutations in the PRKRA gene, which encodes the protein PACT. PACT activates protein kinase R (PKR) in response to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. In DYT-PRKRA patient cells, the PACT-PKR interaction is enhanced, increasing sensitivity to ER stress-induced apoptosis. The canonical protein kinase activated by ER stress is PKR-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase (PERK), which phosphorylates the subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (eIF2) to initiate the integrated stress response (ISR) and restore cellular homeostasis via the transcription factor ATF4. However, under persistent stress, ATF4 induces CHOP, shifting the adaptive response toward apoptosis. PKR, also activated by ER stress, phosphorylates eIF2, but its contribution to cellular homeostasis remains understudied. This work shows, for the first time, that PKR activation is essential for CHOP induction during ISR, directly linking enhanced apoptosis in DYT-PRKRA cells to prolonged PKR activation and heightened CHOP induction. Strikingly, a small-molecule PKR inhibitor effectively blocks CHOP expression and significantly decreases apoptosis in DYT-PRKRA cells, suggesting PKR inhibition as an effective therapeutic strategy for DYT-PRKRA.

papers.title: Peptide-level assay of protein interaction using combinatorial native and denatured proteolysis
papers.abstract: Protein protein interactions underlie many extracellular defense and protease regulatory processes, yet identifying their structural interfaces directly in complex biological samples remains challenging. Limited proteolysis coupled with mass spectrometry provides peptide level readouts of local protease accessibility, but linking condition dependent peptide recovery to structural regions in endogenous proteomes requires complementary analysis. Here, we report peptide level assay of protein interaction (PLAPI) using combinatorial native and denatured proteolysis. A single human serum specimen was analyzed in three paired technical preparations using brief trypsin digestion under native conditions and extended digestion after denaturation, followed by isotopic diethyl labeling and LCMS/MS. Applying a 2 of 3 detection rule yielded 920 denatured only peptides and 124 peptides detected under both conditions, with no native only peptides. Mapping to the reference structures placed 13 denatured only C3b peptides at the Factor B binding interface and identified multiple denatured only A2M intersubunit contact regions. Within the A2M bait region, adjacent peptides exhibited different detection patterns; two were detected under both conditions, whereas one was detected only after denaturation. STRING association and enrichment analyses linked the candidate proteins to extracellular defense and protease regulation. These results indicate that PLAPI can provide peptide level evidence for prioritizing structural regions in complex serum samples and guide focused follow up analyses.

papers.title: GENE FLOW AND CONSERVATION GENOMICS OF DUDLEYA ABRAMSII SSP. SETCHELLII, AN ENDANGERED SUCCULENT IN SANTA CLARA COUNTY
papers.abstract: Understanding how gene flow shapes the distribution of genetic variation is essential for the conservation of rare and geographically restricted species. We investigated genomic structure, clonality, and mechanisms of gene flow in the federally endangered, serpentine endemic Dudleya abramsii ssp. setchellii (Jeps.) Moran using low-coverage whole-genome resequencing of 52 individuals representing 13 populations of D. a. ssp. setchellii, four populations of the geographically adjacent D. cymosa (Lem.) Britton & Rose, and two other subspecies of D. abramsii from San Luis Obispo County. Genome-wide comparisons were combined with analyses of clonality, isolation by distance, principal component analysis, phylogenetic reconstruction, pollinator observations, and a controlled seed dispersal experiment. Strong isolation by distance was detected both within a focal population and among populations across the species' range, indicating that genetic differentiation increases predictably with geographic separation. Clonal reproduction was present, but restricted to individuals separated by only a few centimeters, contributing little to broader spatial genetic structure. Genomic analyses recovered D. a. ssp. setchellii as a distinct lineage exhibiting geographic subdivision within the species and identified a putative hybrid with D. cymosa. Field observations identified bumblebees as the dominant floral visitors, suggesting the potential for pollen-mediated gene flow, whereas a controlled seed dispersal experiment showed that most seeds traveled only a few meters under the artifically optimal experimental wind conditions. Together, these results suggest that limited seed dispersal may contribute to the pronounced spatial genetic structure observed in this serpentine endemic, although the relative contributions of pollen-mediated gene flow, geographic isolation, and genetic drift remain unresolved. These findings provide a genomic framework for conservation and identify geographically structured populations (east vs. west of Coyote Valley) as important units for long-term management.

papers.title: Heat Shock Transcription Factor B1 Coordinates Distinct bHLH Modules to Orchestrate Land Plant Adaptation
papers.abstract: Adaptation to terrestrial environments required the evolution of morphological structures, such as rhizoids and air pores, and robust tolerance mechanisms to environmental stress. While these innovations are well-described, the regulatory logic coordinating development with stress signaling during this transition remains largely unknown. Here, we identify Heat Shock Transcription Factor B1 (HSFB1) as a central evolutionary node that bridges this gap in Marchantia polymorpha. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) and gene regulatory network analysis, we reveal that MpHSFB1 is required to activate cell-type-specific programs for terrestrial adaptation, functioning via the regulation of cytokinin and reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis. We find that MpHSFB1 functions through a modular logic: it co-opts a specific set of bHLH transcription factors (including MpbHLH21/40) to drive developmental morphogenesis, while recruiting a distinct partner (MpbHLH51) to confer resistance to prolonged heat stress. This functional uncoupling allows a single ancestral regulator to manage disparate physiological needs. By reconstructing HSFB1 regulons across diverse plant lineages, we propose that MpHSFB1 acted as an ancestral pleiotropic hub that was effectively rewired and subfunctionalized in later angiosperm lineages for land plant evolution.

papers.title: Tet2-Clonal Hematopoiesis Promotes Whereas Dnmt3a-CH Inhibits Breast Cancer Progression During Aging
papers.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) driven by somatic mutations in blood cells increases with age and is associated with adverse outcomes in cancer patients. How CHIP mutations influence solid tumor progression remains unclear. Using inducible murine models of Dnmt3a- or Tet2-mutant CHIP combined with orthotopic syngeneic breast cancer models, we demonstrate that upon aging Dnmt3a-mutant CHIP prevents whereas Tet2-mutant CHIP drives breast cancer progression. Dnmt3a-mutant immune infiltrates established interferon-mediated MHCIIhigh tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) that supported cytotoxic CD8+ T cell-mediated tumor rejection. In contrast, Tet2-mutant TAMs exhibited an inflammatory, immunosuppressive phenotype characterized by increased IL-1 and CXCL2 production, reduced MHCII expression, and impaired T cell recruitment and activation. Therapeutic blockade of IL-1R1 or CXCR2 reduced tumor progression in aged Tet2-mutant CHIP mice and partially restored anti-tumor immunity. These findings establish that the effects of CHIP on cancer are mutation- and age-dependent and identify IL-1/CXCL2-driven inflammation as a therapeutic vulnerability of tumor-promoting Tet2-mutant CHIP.

papers.title: Towards Understanding the Microenvironmental Control of Reindeer Antler Regeneration
papers.abstract: Deer antlers are the only mammalian appendages capable of complete periodic regeneration and therefore provide a natural model for investigating mechanisms of skeletal regeneration. However, current knowledge of the structural and molecular characteristics of the regenerative antler microenvironment remains incomplete. Here, we compared antler tip and antler base tissues from Rangifer tarandus (reindeer) with mature metacarpal cortical bone using structural, compositional, histological, and proteomic analyses. Antler tissues exhibited smaller and less crystalline apatite structures, elevated carbonate substitution, and higher organic matrix content compared with metacarpal bone, indicating an immature mineral phase. Antlers also exhibited lower bone mineral density, greater porosity, reduced bone volume fraction, and greater trabecular separation, particularly in central regions, consistent with a dynamic remodeling microenvironment. Histological examination revealed abundant active osteons and extensive osteoid seams in antler tissues, whereas metacarpal bone predominantly comprised mature lamellar bone with limited remodeling activity. Proteomic profiling identified distinct extracellular matrix signatures between antler and metacarpal tissues. Metacarpal bone was enriched in proteins associated with skeletal homeostasis, mechanotransduction, and bone remodeling, whereas antler tissues were enriched in proteins involved in extracellular matrix reorganization, metabolic adaptation, and regeneration. Collectively, these findings indicate that reindeer antlers possess a specialized regenerative skeletal microenvironment characterized by immature mineral organization, active remodeling, and distinct molecular signatures associated with rapid tissue growth. These results provide new insights into the biological basis of mammalian appendage regeneration and may facilitate the development of regenerative strategies for bone repair and skeletal tissue engineering.

papers.title: Neural regulation of hatching in amphibians
papers.abstract: Many animal embryos hatch in response to threats or opportunities, yet how cue sensing activates hatching is unknown. We screened red-eyed treefrog (Agalychnis callidryas) eggs in the field with small molecules to discover that the neurotransmitter acetylcholine is a key mediator of hatching enzyme release. Using behavioral pharmacology, microscopy, and transcriptional profiling we identify direct cholinergic input on hatching gland cells that triggers enzyme release for egg rupture, and serotonergic transduction of embryonic hypoxia sensing. Independent hypoxia-sensing and mechanosensory predation-detection pathways converge on a hatching decision that elicits acetylcholine-dependent enzyme release and coordinated hatching-specific behavior. Cholinergic regulation of hatching enzyme release is conserved in a distantly related frog and salamander, suggesting a shared ancestral hatching mechanism. These results provide a neural basis for hatching plasticity which may have contributed to the evolution of diverse hatching modes in amphibians.

papers.title: Co-aggregation of pre-conditioned cell populations drives controlled lineage bias and formation of gut tube-like structures in human stem cell-based embryo models
papers.abstract: Human stem cell-based embryo models (hSCBEMs) provide a powerful platform for investigating post-implantation human embryo development but are frequently hindered by variability in growth and morphogenesis as well as incomplete lineage representations. Here, we present a modular hSCBEM aggregation approach based on co-aggregation of differentially pre-conditioned, human pluripotent stem cell derived cells pools. Using this strategy, we generated hSCBEM with consistent morphotypes that targets robust morphogenesis of gut tube-like structures in combination with mesodermal lineages. Our findings demonstrate that co-aggregating defined cellular heterogeneity represents a versatile approach to specifically guide self-organization in hSCBEMs while improving reproducibility and developmental fidelity. The approach provides a robust platform for supervised morphogenesis in hSCBEMs.

papers.title: HERC1-mediated orphan subunit quality control maintains proteasome homeostasis and is disrupted in HERC1-associated neurodevelopmental disease
papers.abstract: Biallelic hypomorphic variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase HERC1 cause a neurological disorder clinically characterized by macrocephaly, dysmorphic facies, and psychomotor delay. Identifying the substrates of HERC1 is essential for understanding its biological functions and the mechanisms underlying disease-associated variants. To address this, we performed a quantitative proteomic analysis using biotinylated ubiquitin to identify HERC1 targets and examine their regulation in cells expressing HERC1 with or without ubiquitin ligase activity. This approach revealed a broad set of HERC1-dependent ubiquitylation substrates, including proteins from major multiprotein complexes such as the proteasome, the translation initiation machinery, and pathways involved in cell metabolism. Focusing on the proteasome, the most prominently represented complex, we identified several regulatory particle subunits, including PSMC6, PSME1, and PSME2. Specifically, within the 19S regulatory particle, we demonstrated that ubiquitylation of the PSMC6 subunit involves the formation of K48-linked polyubiquitin chains and depends on HERC1 activity. Other 19S subunits, such as PSMC2, PSMC4, and PSMC5, undergo a similar modification. Mechanistically, we show that HERC1 selectively recognizes unassembled subunits, promotes their ubiquitylation, and targets them for proteasomal degradation. Notably, in HERC1-deficient cells, disruption of this mechanism impaired proteasomal activity. At the disease level, quantitative proteomic analysis of the pathogenic HERC1 variant c.1448G>A (p.Gly483Glu) likewise identified altered ubiquitylation of proteasome subunits and components of the translation initiation machinery. Biochemical analyses further revealed impaired ubiquitylation of PSMC6 by the mutant HERC1 protein, associated with a loss of interaction between HERC1 and PSMC6. Together, these findings establish a link between HERC1-associated neurological disorders and defective ubiquitylation pathways. They elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which HERC1 regulates proteostasis and demonstrate how disruption of these processes contributes to disease pathogenesis, thereby highlighting potential avenues for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Endogenous expression of mutant RagC in mice results in early-onset dilated cardiomyopathy with features of the Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome
papers.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a severe heart condition often linked to arrhythmias, clots, and heart failure, for which treatments are not yet curative. Recently, de novo mutations in genes encoding components of the Rag GTPase nutrient signaling pathway, particularly in RRAGC, have been found in unrelated patients with a severe, early-onset DCM syndrome called Long-Olsen-Distelmaier. Cancer cell lines, hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and zebrafish have been used to study this Ragopathy, but a mammalian model to investigate this syndrome has not been generated. Here, we show that mice engineered to endogenously express mutations in Serine 74 (orthologous to the Serine 75 mutated in patients), exhibit early-onset features of DCM with decreased heart size, fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction and aortic insufficiency, characteristics reminiscent of the human syndrome. Moreover, Rragc-mutant hearts display decreased left ventricular mass and interventricular septum. Endogenous heterozygous expression of Rragc mutant variants result in a milder, sublethal defective physiological cardiac growth with increased systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Mechanistically, active RagC does not cause abnormal increase in cardiomyocyte size, but leads to suppressed transcriptional activity of Tfeb and alterations in cardiomyocyte metabolism. Transcriptional profiling of neonatal mutant hearts reveals multiple signatures of impaired mitochondrial activity. Ex vivo and in vitro analyses of murine cardiomyocyte mitochondria from Rragc-mutant mice show suppressed mitochondrial respiration, disturbed complex IV multimerization and super-complex organization. These data point to abnormal early postnatal heart metabolism by deregulated nutrient - Rag GTPase signaling with a potential molecular explanation to the early onset of DCM in patients with de novo missense mutations in RRAGC, and suggests the relevance of early metabolic interventions in conditions with altered nutrient signaling

papers.title: The absence of microbiome in germ-free mice exacerbates the pathogenicity of mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 MA10
papers.abstract: Germ-free mice, which are devoid of microbiota, provide a powerful system to define the contribution of the microbiome to host responses during infection. Severe COVID-19 outcomes are associated with multiple comorbidities that are themselves characterized by microbiome dysbiosis; however, the causal role of the microbiota in SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis remains poorly understood. Here, we use germ-free mouse models to evaluate the impact of the microbiome on disease severity following infection with mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 MA10. Comparison with conventionally housed mice revealed that the absence of the microbiome markedly exacerbates SARS-CoV-2-induced disease in both C57BL/6 and Swiss Webster backgrounds. Germ-free mice exhibited greater weight loss, impaired lung function, worsened pulmonary pathology, and pronounced alterations in circulating cytokine and chemokine profiles compared with conventional controls. These findings show that resident microbiota limit SARS-CoV-2 pathogenicity and establish germ-free COVID-19 models as a powerful platform to identify protective microbial taxa and microbiota-based interventions to reduce severe disease.

papers.title: Divergent methane production and microbial community responses to carbon enrichment in freshwater wetland sediments
papers.abstract: Methane (CH4) accumulation in wetland sediments reflects interactions among organic matter, sediment chemistry, and microbial communities. We combined depth-resolved field characterization across four wetland habitats in northern Israel with complementary incubations to examine methane accumulation and responses to labile-carbon enrichment. Sediment cores were characterized using Rock-Eval analysis, porewater chemistry, oxygen profiling at three sites, and mcrA amplicon sequencing. High CH4 concentrations occurred under contrasting conditions: Ein Nimfit (EN) contained approximately 12% total organic carbon and reached 2.1 mM CH4, whereas Ein Afek site EA2 contained approximately 5% carbon and accumulated 0.7-1.7 mM CH4. Both showed sulfate depletion, but EN exhibited pronounced sulfide accumulation, whereas EA2 showed greater dissolved iron and nutrient enrichment. Their classified methanogenic assemblages also differed. EA1 remained methane poor despite increasing carbon content with depth, while EA3 combined low carbon content and CH4 accumulation with detectable methanogens and lower methanogenic diversity. In a 36-day bottle experiments using sediments from two of the four wetland habitats, sucrose-amended EA3 exhibited a transient maximum of 18.8 mmol collected CH4 kg-1 wet sediment during Days 22-29, whereas EN reached its highest collected amount during Days 29-36. Methane proportions increased before the large output increase in EA3 but remained comparatively stable and high in EN. Soluble chemical oxygen demand trajectories and microbial community changes also differed. These findings identify distinct biogeochemical settings supporting methane accumulation and demonstrate methanogenic potential in low-CH4 sediment, emphasizing the complementary information provided by field profiles, microbial characterization, and exploratory enrichment experiments.

papers.title: Reverse Transcription Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Combined with Lateral Flow Assay (RT-LAMP-LFA) for Rapid Detection of the 2026 Bundibugyo Virus (BDBV) Outbreak Strain
papers.abstract: Making accurate diagnosis is a critical first step in patient management and control for emerging and re-emerging disease outbreaks. Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) is a filovirus that causes Ebola disease, and the 2026 outbreak highlights the need for rapid diagnostic approaches that can be deployed in settings with limited laboratory infrastructure. Here, we developed a reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification-lateral flow assay (RT-LAMP-LFA) for rapid detection of the 2026 BDBV outbreak strain. LAMP primers were designed based on the genome sequence of the 2026 outbreak strain, and the conservation of the primer binding sites among all available 2026 outbreak genomes was confirmed in silico. LAMP primers were evaluated for analytical specificity and sensitivity using in vitro-transcribed RNA (ivtRNA) from BDBV and other filoviruses, as well as RNA derived from arboviruses and mammalian cells. Amplification products were detected using a Chromatography-Printed Array Strip (C-PAS) lateral flow platform. The newly designed primers specifically detected the presence of BDBV RNA without nonspecific amplification of the other viral or cellular RNA samples tested. Consistent amplification was observed down to 103 copies per reaction. In addition, BDBV viral RNA was successfully amplified, and the amplification products were detected using C-PAS, with the total workflow being completed within 25 min. These findings demonstrate the analytical specificity and sensitivity of the developed RT-LAMP-LFA assay and its compatibility with rapid visual lateral flow detection, supporting its potential application as a point-of-care approach for BDBV detection.

papers.title: Antagonism between sugar-dependent O-fucosylation and BIN2-mediated phosphorylation regulates metabolism and growth in Arabidopsis
papers.abstract: Coordinating sugar sensing, hormone signaling, and carbon metabolism is crucial for plant growth and environmental acclimation. Brassinosteroid (BR)-dependent phosphorylation and sugar-dependent O-glycosylation modify overlapping sets of proteins, but how these modifications co-regulate protein functions remains unknown. Here, we show that SPINDLY (SPY)-catalyzed O-fucosylation competes with BIN2-mediated phosphorylation and antagonistically regulates phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (PCK1), a key gluconeogenic enzyme. SPY associates with and O-fucosylates PCK1 within a peptide containing Ser-62 and Thr-66, two BIN2 phosphorylation sites that regulate PCK1 activity, preventing its phosphorylation by BIN2. PCK1 O-fucosylation and phosphorylation exclude each other and oppositely affect PCK1 activity in vivo. The spy mutants show increased PCK1 phosphorylation, reduced PCK activity, and impaired hypocotyl elongation; BR or BIN2 inhibitor treatments suppressed these phenotypes, indicating that these spy effects result from increased BIN2 phosphorylation. Together, these results reveal functional antagonism between SPY/O-fucosylation and BIN2/phosphorylation in regulating metabolism and growth

papers.title: Genome-wide latitudinal variation associated with defence and reproductive pathways linked to Norway spruce adaptation
papers.abstract: Environmental cues modulate the natural variations in genes that outline local adaptation in plants for optimal survival. Genome-wide analysis using exome capture dataset in Norway spruce (Picea abies L. Kast) in Sweden revealed natural allelic variation in coding regions of genes associated with defence and reproductive pathways that follow a latitudinal cline, despite of the weak population structure with a low genetic differentiation. Steepest clines in the allele frequencies of missense SNPs from coding region (cSNPs) were detected in 60S RIBOSOMAL PROTEIN L18 (RPL18C), a gene involved in plant survival and defence/stress responses and LONG AFTER FAR-RED 3 (LAF3) that mediates light responses. This was closely followed by cline in ZINC 4 FINGER DNA 3'-PHOSPHOESTERASE (ZDP), involved in DNA repair and DNA demethylation pathways. Flowering genes that displayed latitudinal cline in cSNPs included BARELY ANY MERISTEM 1 (BAM1), REDUCED VERNALIZATION RESPONSE 1 (VRN1), FLOWERING CONTROL LOCUS A (FCA) and TERMINAL FLOWER 1 (TFL1) among few others. These variations may contribute to differential functioning of the defence/flowering genes, enabling the tree to thrive at its best under given local environmental conditions. The clines provide evidence towards local adaptation in these Norway spruce populations across Sweden; it coincides with the latitudinal variation in climatic conditions including temperature, day length and light quality, along with existing cline e.g. differential growth and defence response, and bud-burst/bud-set. The knowledge can be applied in forest industry to design future sustainable breeding strategies e.g. assisted migration, in the context of inevitable climate change.

papers.title: Heat-induced increases in xylem vulnerability: Experimental evidence and possible mechanisms
papers.abstract: Hotter droughts driven by global warming are increasing tree mortality worldwide. Here, we propose a theoretical framework that explains how dissolved gas affects the stability of bubbles in xylem sap, and shows that in the presence of gas, sudden increases in temperature can accelerate embolism formation. We then provide experimental evidence that heat exposure can change xylem vulnerability to drought. Using data from seven Australian and European tree species, we assessed how elevated temperature (+15 and +20 {degrees}C above ambient) affects both xylem embolism resistance, measured with the Optical Vulnerability Technique, and VPD-corrected drying times. We found evidence for reduced embolism resistance and accelerated dehydration in heat-exposed plants. On average, trees reached the water potential at 50% loss of xylem function at 0.73 MPa less negative water potentials and 7.8 kPa h earlier, though responses were highly species-specific, and credibly different from zero only in the Australian species. Our results are consistent with the proposed framework and suggest that embolism resistance may not be a static trait, which has important repercussions for studies of plant vulnerability to drought. Further studies are necessary to assess the potential effects of heat-induced reductions in embolism resistance on tree mortality during heatwaves.

papers.title: Ancestral polyploidy and non-linear dosage shifts define the photosynthetic transition in the Heliantheae alliance
papers.abstract: Whole-genome duplications (WGDs) have played a central role in plant evolutionary innovation, yet their genome-wide influence on complex physiological traits such as carbon-concentrating mechanisms (CCMs) remains poorly resolved. Here, we present high-quality genome assemblies and annotations for 35 species within the Heliantheae alliance (Asteraceae), spanning the complex photosynthetic spectrum from C3 to C4. Ks-based analyses combined with gene tree-species tree reconciliation identified a shared paleopolyploid event (WGD-2) ~30 million years ago. Using phylogenetically informed association mapping with these species, we detected 451 functional MapMan BINs with copy number variation significantly associated with interspecific variation in the CO2 compensation point. Notably, 303 of these BINs contain greater than 10% WGD-2-derived genes, indicating a strong enrichment of duplicated loci within photosynthetically relevant functional modules. Effect-size analysis revealed that the C3-to-C4 transition is governed by threshold-dependent genomic architecture rather than gradual additive change. Substantial expansions in key transcription factor modules, including HD-ZIP, HSF, LOB, and TCP, were associated with strong non-linear physiological shifts, consistent with genomic tipping points. By integrating comparative genomics, physiological trait variation, and evolutionary analysis, this study establishes a mechanistic link between ancient polyploidy and contemporary photosynthetic diversification. These findings provide a framework for understanding the genetic basis of carbon concentrating mechanism evolution and inform future optimization of photosynthetic efficiency in Asteraceae crops such as sunflower.

papers.title: Drought Response and Recovery in Wild, Feral, and Domesticated Brassica rapa: Implications for Crop Climate Resilience
papers.abstract: Drought poses a serious threat to agricultural production and food security. Wild relatives of crops, including pre-domesticated and feral varieties, contain genetic diversity that can serve as a breeding resource for increasing desirable crop traits such as drought resilience, but little is known about the relative ability of wild varieties to cope with climate change in most species. In this study, we investigated the drought response of wild, feral, and domesticated varieties of Brassica rapa, an important crop and model species. Twenty-five accessions were subjected to experimental drought and recovery, and variation in traits such as biomass retention, photosynthetic rate, and water use efficiency were quantified. We found several wild accessions of B. rapa had high biomass retention under drought and full recovery of maximum assimilation rate after rewatering, challenging the assumption that feralization produces stress-resilient phenotypes and suggesting that populations of wild crop progenitors are especially promising reservoirs of drought-response diversity. Our results also showed taproot biomass was positively associated with water use efficiency. Our findings provide candidate traits and genotypes for agricultural breeding aimed at increasing drought resilience in domesticated B. rapa cultivars and give insights into evolution under domestication and feralization in the context of climate change.
